findings.evidence: Hovering the logo renders rgb(0,71,143) on rgb(26,26,26), a 1.90:1 contrast ratio; the generic a:hover/a:focus rule overrides the white logo state.
findings.userImpact: Keyboard and mouse users lose the site name when they focus or hover the logo; low-vision users cannot read it.
findings.fix: Add scoped .ontario-header__logo:hover and :focus rules that retain white or use another color with at least 3:1 contrast on black.

findings.evidence: At a 320 CSS px viewport, documentElement.scrollWidth is 695px because the data table has no horizontal scroll region.
findings.userImpact: Users zoomed to 400% must scroll horizontally to read the page, not only the table.
findings.fix: Wrap the table in a keyboard-focusable region with overflow-x:auto and label it from the caption.

findings.evidence: After a server-side validation failure, all four controls have null aria-describedby and the validation spans have no explicit IDs. Client validation adds associations only when JavaScript succeeds.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader users do not hear the server-rendered error when revisiting an invalid field.
findings.fix: Give each validation span a stable ID and point the associated control's aria-describedby to it.

findings.evidence: aria-invalid remains null on every invalid control in both client and server error states.
findings.userImpact: Screen readers do not announce that each rejected field is invalid.
findings.fix: Render aria-invalid from ModelState and configure client validation to set and clear the same state.

findings.evidence: The ModelOnly summary is empty for field errors, has no tabindex, receives no focus, and the document title remains New service request.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader users are not told that submission failed or how many fields need attention.
findings.fix: Render a linked error summary, focus it after failed POST, and prefix the document title with Error.

findings.evidence: All four Model properties are required, but every rendered control has required=false and null aria-required, and no visible instruction identifies required fields.
findings.userImpact: Users learn that fields are mandatory only after a failed submission.
findings.fix: Add visible required wording and required or aria-required=true to each control.
findings.notes: Required wording should receive content review.

findings.evidence: Focused controls render a 2.67px rgb(255,208,39) outline on white with no box shadow; yellow-on-white is 1.47:1 and the blue border change is 2.27:1.
findings.userImpact: Low-vision keyboard users struggle to see which form field has focus.
findings.fix: Use a dark 3px focus ring and keep yellow only as an outer halo.

findings.evidence: At a 320 CSS px viewport, the unbroken request ID makes documentElement.scrollWidth 367px.
findings.userImpact: Zoomed users must scroll sideways to read the support reference.

findings.evidence: No rendered page has an element with aria-current=page.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader and sighted users cannot identify the current section from navigation state.
findings.fix: Render aria-current=page on the matching navigation link.

findings.evidence: The success state renders #submission-confirmation but keeps the title New service request and does not focus its heading.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader users are not immediately told that the request succeeded.
findings.fix: Set a Request submitted title and focus a tabindex=-1 confirmation heading on load.

findings.evidence: The primary navigation and footer each expose a link named Privacy, but they lead to different destinations.
findings.userImpact: A screen reader links list contains two indistinguishable Privacy entries.
findings.fix: Choose distinct wording, such as Ontario.ca privacy statement or Demo privacy notice, or explicitly accept landmark context.

findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, button transition-duration remains 0.15s for background, color, and border because no reduced-motion media block exists.
findings.userImpact: Users who request reduced motion still receive interaction transitions.
findings.fix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block that reduces transitions and animations to 0.01ms and disables smooth scrolling.
findings.notes: Advisory WCAG AAA item; it does not block the WCAG 2.2 AA verdict.
